assuranceCeiling.rationale: Critical data-preserving schema-upgrade rehearsal with occupied tenant records can reveal failures hidden by empty installation. Reuse all original 78 Git-pinned migrations in two committed stages on identity-verified disposable Docker PostgreSQL17; block hosted mutations and claims about real Auth-signed JWT, recovery/restore, schema parity or deployment.

acceptanceCriteria: Two separate real PG17 committed states: after original 0046 legacy baseline, and after original 0047..0058 plus 19 historical source migrations.
At least one nonzero prior Office thread with preserved exact ID, tenant and user, positive before/after upgrade; modern participant row backfill post-upgrade.
Fault-injection rollback from legacy state fails with ON_ERROR_STOP and proves original legacy table/policy remains without partially applied new participant table.
No source SQL copied with modifications; original 78 pinned Git blobs reused, and stage2 does not execute empty-target preflight or replay old baseline.
All operations local disposable PG17 with real native results; hosted untouched, signed Supabase JWT/Data API unproven.
Security/Quality/TypeScript/Build, exact-head Truth/Lifecycle and PR Draft, no merge.
invariants: Never modify original 59 baseline SQL files or 19 main migration source files.
Require positive legacy data; cannot mark success if data missing before or after.
Do not skip, duplicate, reorder or drop any of 78 pinned source files.
Only Docker PG17 fixture with peer identity guard; fail if inherited hosted DB URLs.
Fault transaction must rollback without persistence, no destructive hosted executor.
Core #1186 and #1228 remain open pending migration provenance and provider API.
forbiddenStates: Only empty database proves upgrade with no occupied records.
The old user or customer thread disappears, or duplicate fixture rows hide loss.
Any historical migration altered in generated replay.

A failed stage2 leaves half the schema mutated or participants present.
A local proof is described as signed JWT, production readiness or live Fresh Install acceptance.

failureModes: Existing pre-0047 Office data violates a new 0048 CHECK or participant FK.
Stage2 accidentally replays 0001 and drops old rows.
Office helper or GRANT migration requires main historical predecessor objects in exact order.
A rollback test passes because no legacy records existed.

edgeCases: The original 0001 baseline has different office_threads column definitions before 0048.
Auth user trigger exists after stage1 and may materialize profile rows.
A legacy customer thread with no participant and nonnull creator is backfilled by 0048.
Legacy tenant is Alap, retains customer case after upgrade.

challenge.scenario: A historic customer Office record is absent from initial seed and the upgrade returns zero rows without error.
challenge.finding: An empty fixture is not evidence of safe legacy migration.
challenge.resolution: Require a nonzero known thread ID before and after and reject missing positive control.

challenge.scenario: The second stage reruns an earlier CREATE statement and reinitializes application tables.
challenge.finding: Baseline replay would overwrite or collide with existing tenant records.
challenge.resolution: Split exactly once at original 0047 marker and prohibit all pre-0047 source markers in upgrade.

challenge.scenario: A generated SQL file has comments for all 78 migrations but silently drops actual source bytes.
challenge.finding: Source marker counting alone is not a SQL validity proof.
challenge.resolution: Compare full canonical SQL pieces byte-for-byte and enforce manifest Git blob integrity before real psql execution.

challenge.scenario: Legacy Office creators are backfilled incorrectly after 0048 participant creation.
challenge.finding: Customer Office historical visibility may be lost without an explicit participant row.
challenge.resolution: Require 0048 real source-trigger backfill for known creator and positive customer access control.

challenge.scenario: The second transaction fails halfway but validators inspect data left by a previous successful run.
challenge.finding: Uncleared local state could conceal rollback regression.
challenge.resolution: Use separate Docker database or transaction-local injected failure with hard peer check and explicit catalog asserts.

challenge.scenario: An obsolete source from main is appended after new migration and supersedes Pro-only Office enforcement.
challenge.finding: Migration order matters beyond simple filename sort.
challenge.resolution: Reuse the earlier Git SHA pinned source manifest with main predecessors before 0055 and FK follow-up before 0058.

challenge.scenario: A local role GUC is mistaken for managed PostgREST and signed provider JWT proof.
challenge.finding: Authentication source boundary would be falsely elevated to release.
challenge.resolution: Verdict states local disposable fixture only with managed JWT/API/Storage false.

challenge.scenario: The old customer record survives but its tenant membership or plan is changed by the upgrade.
challenge.finding: Row-existence-only checks miss data mutation and cross-tenant rebind.
challenge.resolution: Assert exact row instance_id, owner id, subscription plan and related tenancy identifiers on both sides of upgrade.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The proven source-authentic 78 SQL replay currently runs only on an empty PostgreSQL17 database, whereas the active managed Fresh Install contains an existing legacy Office schema with empty migration history. A naïve upgrade can delete tenant rows, break participant backfill, fail privacy policies or misapply dependencies. Split verified original source SQL at historical 0047 and prove occupied state survives the forward-only upgrade without touching hosted data.
